messages.title: Which Event Is Actually Newer?
messages.subtitle: A later delivery can carry older state. Find the authority that orders changes to one shipment.
messages.property: For one shipment, a projected state must not regress from a newer authoritative revision to an older one.
messages.takeaway: A version field is useful because the source contract gives it authoritative ordering meaning—not because it is named ‘version.’
messages.step.review.title: A late arrival is not necessarily new
messages.step.review.lead: Shipment42 has two source changes. Follow source order and delivery order separately before deciding what the projection should store.
messages.step.source-order.title: What did the source say first?
messages.step.source-order.lead: The authoritative source emits E42 at revision 42 (PROCESSING), then E43 at revision 43 (SHIPPED). Its revision contract says 43 supersedes 42 for Shipment42.
messages.step.arrival-order.title: Delivery takes the other route
messages.step.arrival-order.lead: The projection receives E43 before E42. Arrival order is a fact about transport, not evidence that E42 is newer.
messages.step.apply-43.title: Apply the first arrival
messages.step.apply-43.lead: The weak handler applies E43. Shipment42 now reads SHIPPED at revision 43. So far, the projection matches the source's latest state.
messages.step.late-42.title: E42 arrives later
messages.step.late-42.lead: Would applying E42 now overwrite SHIPPED with PROCESSING? Predict the result before advancing.
messages.step.arrival-assumption.title: The hidden assumption
messages.step.arrival-assumption.lead: The handler writes every delivered state. It has no stored authoritative revision to compare, so it treats arrival as permission to overwrite.
messages.step.regression.title: The projection moves backward
messages.step.regression.lead: E42 overwrites E43. Shipment42 ends at PROCESSING, revision 42, even though the source already emitted SHIPPED at revision 43.
messages.step.property.title: Name the property
messages.step.property.lead: For Shipment42, an older authoritative revision must never replace a newer one already applied. The claim is scoped to this entity stream.
messages.step.timestamp.title: Could a timestamp decide?
messages.step.timestamp.lead: Ask who produced the timestamp, which clock it used, and what ordering it guarantees. A larger timestamp is not automatically authoritative source order.
messages.step.source-contract.title: Give revision a meaning
messages.step.source-contract.lead: The source promises unique, monotonically increasing revisions for Shipment42; a larger revision supersedes a smaller one. The projection stores state and applied revision together.
messages.step.apply-43-strong.title: Apply revision 43 atomically
messages.step.apply-43-strong.lead: E43 is newer than the stored revision. Commit SHIPPED and applied revision 43 in one projection mutation.
messages.step.reject-42.title: Reject the stale arrival
messages.step.reject-42.lead: E42 carries revision 42, below the applied revision 43. Keep SHIPPED and revision 43 unchanged; the source contract, not delivery time, justifies that decision.
messages.step.forward-44.title: A genuinely newer event advances
messages.step.forward-44.lead: When the source emits revision 44, a projection at 43 may advance to 44. The guard rejects stale events without freezing progress.
messages.step.duplicate.title: An equal revision is a duplicate
messages.step.duplicate.lead: In a separate run, E43 arrives twice. After the first application, another revision 43 cannot replace it or move it backward.
messages.step.entity-scope.title: Keep comparison inside its stream
messages.step.entity-scope.lead: Shipment42 revision 43 and Shipment99 revision 100 are not globally ordered by those numbers. Independent writers or revision resets need a stronger source contract too.
messages.step.remaining.title: Non-regressing can still be stale
messages.step.remaining.lead: The projection may stay at revision 43 while the source has reached revision 50. Rejecting old arrivals does not prove a read is fresh enough; Case 06 examines that gap.
messages.step.transfer.title: Transfer: a customer profile
messages.step.transfer.lead: Profile revision 109 changes an email after revision 108. If 109 arrives first, should 108 overwrite it? What if the numbers came from unrelated producer-local counters?
messages.step.recap.title: Six questions, one source order
messages.step.recap.lead: Use these questions before treating a version field as an ordering rule.
messages.visual.title: Source Order vs Arrival Order
messages.visual.sourceEvents: E42 · rev 42 · PROCESSING → E43 · rev 43 · SHIPPED
messages.visual.duplicate43: Shipment42 · rev 43 · SHIPPED · repeat E43 ignored
messages.rail.evidenceWeak: The weak projection ends at revision 42 after seeing 43.
messages.rail.evidenceStrong: The source orders revisions for this one shipment.
messages.rail.contractWeak: Apply each arrival without a revision guard.
messages.rail.contractSource: Unique, increasing source revisions per entity; larger supersedes smaller.
messages.rail.contractStrong: Compare revision and commit state with applied revision atomically.
messages.rail.propertyHidden: Which arrival is allowed to replace the projection?
messages.rail.property: An older source revision cannot replace a newer applied revision for the same entity.
messages.challenge.title: Why may the projection reject E42?
messages.challenge.intro: E43 reached the projection before E42. Choose the evidence that actually justifies keeping SHIPPED.
messages.challenge.question: Which contract makes revision 42 stale for Shipment42?
messages.option.sourceRevision: The source assigns monotonic revisions per shipment; 43 supersedes 42.
messages.option.arrival: E43 arrived first, so it must be the newest event.
messages.option.timestamp: The field is called ‘version,’ so its larger number must be newer.
messages.challenge.feedback: The source's per-shipment revision contract establishes the order. Neither arrival time nor a field name can establish it alone.
messages.deepDive.title: What does the revision guard actually promise?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: The minimal regression
messages.deepDive.section1.body: E43 applies first, E42 arrives later, and a blind handler overwrites SHIPPED with PROCESSING. The failure is one entity moving to an older authoritative state.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: The atomic comparison
messages.deepDive.section2.body: Compare the incoming revision with the stored applied revision inside one projection mutation. If it is larger, commit both state and revision; otherwise keep both unchanged.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: When ordering is unnecessary
messages.deepDive.section3.body: A tag set built by set union is commutative: adding tags in either delivery order yields the same final set. Its property does not require rejecting an older arrival.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: Where the number's meaning ends
messages.deepDive.section4.body: The promise applies to one entity stream. Different entities, independent writers, or revision resets need their own ordering contract. Timestamps require an explicit clock and producer guarantee.
messages.deepDive.section5.title: The next question is freshness
messages.deepDive.section5.body: A projection that never goes backward may still lag behind the source. Case 06 asks whether the revision observed by a read is current enough for its purpose.
messages.recap.1: Identity: which entity stream does this event describe?
messages.recap.2: Authority: which source assigns revision meaning?
messages.recap.3: Durability: do state and applied revision commit together?
messages.recap.4: Delivery: can older or duplicate events arrive late?
messages.recap.5: Ordering: which source revision supersedes which?
messages.recap.6: Freshness: is a non-regressing projection current enough?
